belief: “I don’t get to decide what happens to my body. Saying no doesn’t count.”
belief_plain: I don’t get to decide what happens to my body. Saying no doesn’t count
origins: When someone treats your body as if it belonged to them, you can start to believe the treatment. “I don’t get to decide. Saying no doesn’t count.” That is what harm teaches. It is not the truth. Your body is not a possession of another person. A no counts even if it was ignored. A yes that was forced, frightened, or not free was not a real yes. You do not have to describe what happened in order to hold this truth. A counselor can help you practice choice in ordinary, safe ways. If you are not safe right now, call 911. You can also call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233. If a child is being hurt, call Childhelp at 1-800-422-4453. A counselor can help you at a pace that is safe. You do not have to do this alone, or all at once.
self: I do not get a vote about my own body.
Saying no just makes it worse, so it does not count.
My body is already ruined, so boundaries are pointless.
Other people’s wants matter more than my no.
God expects me to submit even when I am afraid.
replacement: My body is not someone else’s to decide about. My no counts, even if it was ignored.
